composers_checked.name: Shostakovich, Dmitri
composers_checked.note: All 21 IMSLP pages judged (15 quartets, 2 piano trios, quintet, octet, Two Pieces, collection page); gap check against the Wikipedia work list added the Blok Romances (Op. 127) and the 1961 Quartet Movement in E-flat major (unfinished, recorded by Danel and Asasello). Not added: arrangements by others (Barshai's chamber symphonies, Atovmyan's and Tsyganov's pieces), the Op. 140 and Op. 143 songs (chamber orchestra / voice and piano).

composers_checked.name: Weinberg, Mieczysław
composers_checked.note: No IMSLP pages (modern composer): list from the Wikipedia work list. All 17 string quartets (Danel/cpo and Arcadia/Chandos cycles), Aria, Capriccio, Improvisation and Romance, Piano Quintet, Piano Trio, String Trio, Trio Op. 127 and Three Palms kept. Left out: Chamber Symphonies 1-4 (string orchestra), duos and solos; the Op. 141 recomposition of No. 1 is one entry with Op. 2.

composers_checked.name: Schnittke, Alfred
composers_checked.note: No IMSLP pages (modern composer): list from the Wikipedia work list and recordings. Four quartets, Canon, Variations, Piano Quintet, Piano Quartet, String Trio, Piano Trio (composer's own version), Septet, Serenade, Three Madrigals, Dialogue, Hymns I, III, IV kept. Not added: Hymn II (duo), Concerto Grosso Nos. 1 and 3 and Moz-Art (string orchestra), duos.

composers_checked.name: Gubaidulina, Sofia
composers_checked.note: No IMSLP pages (modern composer). Four quartets, B-A-C-H Reflections, Piano Quintet, String Trio, Quaternion, Silenzio, Quasi hoquetus, Meditation, Garden of Joys and Sorrows, Perception, Hommage a T.S. Eliot kept. Not added (no recording found or scoring unconfirmed): Ein Walzerpass (piano and string quintet), Mirage: The Dancing Sun (8 cellos), Five Etudes (harp, double bass, percussion), Tartarische Tanz, Concordanza (recorded, scoring not confirmed), Detto II (cello and ensemble), Verwandlung, Ravvedimento; duos and string-orchestra works are out of scope.

composers_checked.name: Ustvolskaya, Galina

Composition No. 2 'Dies irae' (eight double basses, piano, wooden cube: ten players) is out of scope; Composition Nos. 1 and 3 have no strings; the violin and cello duos are duos.

note: EVIDENCE: Deezer album and track lists (labels, years, timings; album ids in sources) are the main recording evidence, with Apple Music lookups (composerTerm searches for the lesser-known composers), MusicBrainz work lists (Weinberg), Wikipedia work lists (en for all, ru for Shebalin, Khachaturian, Shchedrin) and, via search results, IRCAM/Boosey entries (Gubaidulina's Perception and Hommage a T.S. Eliot, Schnittke's Piano Trio and Dialog). Naxos Library and Presto were not used; Discogs refused WebFetch. Only Shostakovich (21 pages) and Shebalin (6) have IMSLP pages; every other work is added from work lists plus recordings. VIOLIN CATALOGUE: none of the nine `violin` entries falls in scope, so no violin_id: Weinberg Op. 69, Denisov 1958 and Schnittke's Prelude and Moz-Art are duos; Concerto Grosso Nos. 1 and 3 and Moz-Art a la Haydn are for strings; Atovmyan's Five Pieces for 2 violins and piano is an arrangement by another; the cadenzas are no work. OWNER MAY RULE: (1) voice-with-ensemble works kept under the vocal rule: Shostakovich's Blok Romances, Weinberg's Three Palms, Schnittke's Three Madrigals, Gubaidulina's Perception (two voices, seven strings, tape: nine players) and Hommage a T.S. Eliot (soprano and octet: nine players), Ustvolskaya's Symphony No. 5 (speaker, oboe, trumpet, tuba, violin, wooden cube; titled a symphony); (2) Schnittke's Piano Quartet (1988) is his completion of a Mahler sketch, and his Piano Trio (1992) is his own version of the String Trio (confirmed by IRCAM and a BIS booklet via search results); (3) Popov's Quartet-Symphony has one recording, by Quartet Berlin-Tokyo on its own label (medium). WEAK SPOTS: Weinberg's Improvisation and Romance has no confirmed date; Schnittke's Septet and Serenade durations come from one CD each (the Serenade CD may hold only part of the work), and Dialogue gives the publisher's 18 minutes against 12:55 on the Toccata CD; Shebalin Nos. 2-4 rest on the Olympia/Krasni set (listings seen only in search summaries); Tishchenko's Op. 8 and Op. 90 keys are not given because no source printed them; Weinberg's quartet keys come from recording track titles. NOT ADDED (no recording or performance found, or scoring unconfirmed): Denisov's Piano Trio (1971, Peters, premiere 1972), String Trio (1969), quartets and quintets, Femme et oiseaux; Gubaidulina's Mirage, Walzerpass, Five Etudes, Tartarische Tanz, Concordanza (recorded, scoring unconfirmed), Detto II; Khachaturian's 1931 quartet; Babajanian's quartets; Shebalin's Nos. 6-8 and String Trio; Popov's 1958 Quintet; Tishchenko's smaller works. Shchedrin and Karayev: no in-scope work found. KEYS: Popov's Quartet-Symphony is given without a key because sources disagree (C major in Wikipedia, C minor in The Strad, The WholeNote and VIAF). SOURCES: IMSLP URLs stand for the census records in the input; the pages were not opened separately.
